title_guess: Credit default swap: protection for a bond investor against default
running_examples: company XYZ Ltd sells a corporate bond to investor A; A buys a CDS from seller B, pays a periodic premium, and B pays A if XYZ defaults

best_moments.why: the red RISK disc lifts off investor A and slides down onto the CDS seller's building: risk transfer shown as an object physically moving from one party to another
the inset of the wide-awake man in bed turns into floating Z's once protection is bought: the purpose of a CDS shown as a feeling (worry → sleep)
a red RISK disc drops over investor A and a callout line runs to the inset of the same man lying awake: whose risk it is, and why it matters, in one glance

weak_moments.why: the core rule (if XYZ defaults, B pays A) arrives as a paragraph; the default event itself is never shown happening (no broken bond, no payout arrow)
the premium is a dotted line with a tiny money icon plus a text box; the 'periodic' part (repeated payments) is not animated
about 27 s of intro with only a character and a title card before the first idea

segments.teaches: hook: an investor who cannot sleep; topic is the credit default swap

elements.what: cartoon man lying wide-eyed in bed on a black background
certificate card stamped CDS with the full name written under it

segments.notes: dark intro; the bed character comes back later as an inset panel that carries the emotional payoff
segments.idea: a bond holder worries about being repaid; CDS is the answer this video explains
segments.shown_as: on a black screen a cartoon man lies awake in bed; a certificate card stamped CDS fades in beside him with its full name; then the screen turns white for the diagram

segments.teaches: XYZ Ltd issues a corporate bond to investor A, who pays cash; A now carries the risk that XYZ may not repay

elements.what: bond certificate travelling from XYZ to A on a cream 'corporate bond' strip
dotted line with a rupee note going back from A to XYZ
red RISK disc dropped over investor A
line from A to a dark inset of the man awake in bed
caption under the inset: A fears XYZ's creditworthiness and a default

segments.notes: risk is an object (red disc) that sits on a person; the inset reuses the intro character
segments.idea: buying a bond means lending to a company, so the buyer bears the risk that the company fails to pay
segments.shown_as: a factory labelled XYZ sends a bond certificate along an arrow to investor A on a cream 'corporate bond' strip while a rupee note travels back above on a dotted line; a red RISK disc then drops over A, and a callout line links A to an inset of the same man lying awake, captioned that he fears a default
segments.example: XYZ Ltd bond bought by investor A

segments.teaches: A buys a credit default swap from seller B; if XYZ defaults, B compensates A, so the default risk moves from A to B

elements.what: tall office building (seller B) below investor A
small CDS certificate on an up-arrow from B to A
'Credit Default Swap' dark chip beside the certificate
rule: if XYZ misses a payment, buyer A is compensated by seller B
red RISK disc moves from A down onto B's building

segments.notes: the risk disc move (about 65-75 s) is the key visual; the payout rule itself is only text
segments.idea: a CDS shifts the risk of a bond default from the bond holder to the CDS seller
segments.shown_as: a CDS certificate rises on an arrow from a tall office building (seller B) up to investor A, tagged 'Credit Default Swap', with a rule paragraph at the side; then the red RISK disc lifts off A and slides down to sit over B's building, leaving A uncovered
segments.example: if XYZ misses a payment, B pays A

segments.teaches: A pays B a periodic fee (premium) for this protection, and can now sleep

elements.what: inset swaps from the awake man to a dark panel of floating Z's
dotted line from A down the right side to B with a small money icon
blue note: A pays a periodic fee to B for protection against XYZ default

segments.notes: emotional before/after (awake → asleep) is the payoff of the whole video
segments.idea: the protection is not free: the buyer pays the seller a regular premium
segments.shown_as: the inset of the wide-awake man is replaced by a dark panel of floating Z's (he now sleeps); a dotted line runs from A down to B carrying a small money icon, with a blue note that A pays a periodic premium for the protection
segments.example: periodic premium from A to B

elements.what: app promo phone over the diagram, then next-video / playlist card

segments.shown_as: promo phone slides up over the diagram, then the channel's next-video card replaces it
